questions.q: To where did the man bring Ezekiel?
questions.a: The man brought Ezekiel into the temple’s Holy Place.

questions.q: How long and how wide was the Holy Place?
questions.a: The Holy Place was 40 cubits long and 20 cubits wide.

questions.q: Where did the man go next?
questions.a: The man went next into an inner room.

questions.q: What did the man call that inner room that was 20 cubits long and 20 cubits wide?
questions.a: He called it the Holy of Holies.

questions.q: How thick was the wall of the temple, and how wide were the side chambers?
questions.a: The wall of the temple was six cubits thick, and the side chambers were four cubits wide.

questions.q: How many side rooms were around the temple building?
questions.a: There were 30 side rooms around the temple building, and each one had two more rooms directly above it.

questions.q: How would someone get to the highest room of the house?
questions.a: To get to the highest room of the house, there were steps that went up through the middle room.

questions.q: How high was the part of the platform that the side rooms stood on?
questions.a: The platform that the side rooms stood on was six long cubits high.

questions.q: How wide was the open space between the side rooms and the other rooms around the temple building?
questions.a: The open space was 20 cubits or 10.8 meters wide all around the temple building.

questions.q: How thick was the outer wall of the side rooms?
questions.a: The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits or 2.7 meters thick.

questions.q: In which direction did each of the two doorways into the side rooms face?
questions.a: One doorway faced north, and the other faced south.

questions.q: How wide and how long was the building on the west side of the courtyard?
questions.a: The building was 70 cubits or 38 meters wide and 90 cubits or 49 meters long.

questions.q: How did the measurements of the length of the temple and the length of the courtyard plus the other building and its walls compare?
questions.a: These measurements were both 100 cubits or 54 meters long.

questions.q: How long was the building on the west side of the western courtyard, including its ledges?
questions.a: It was 100 cubits or 54 meters long.

questions.q: What covered the walls of the three rooms from the floor up to the niches?
questions.a: Wood panels covered the walls from the floor up to the niches.

questions.q: What covered the walls above the entryway, inside and outside, up to the Most Holy Place?
questions.a: Long, thin pieces of wood paneling, each the same size, covered all the walls above the entryway, inside and outside, up to the Most Holy Place.

questions.q: What was carved between each pair of cherubs?
questions.a: A palm tree was carved between each pair of cherubs.

questions.q: What two faces did each cherub have?
questions.a: Each cherub had the face of a man and the face of a young lion.

questions.q: Where were the cherubs and palm trees carved on the wall of the holy place?
questions.a: They were carved from the floor up to the top of the entrance.

questions.q: How did the door frame into the Most Holy Place compare to the door frame into the Holy Place?
questions.a: The door frame into the Most Holy Place was exactly the same as the door frame into the Holy Place.

questions.q: What did the man say about the wooden altar in front of the holy place?
questions.a: The man said that the wooden altar was the table that was in Yahweh’s presence.

questions.q: How many sets of doors did the entrance into the Holy Place and the entrance into the Most Holy Place each have?
questions.a: Each entrance had two sets of doors.

questions.q: How many panels did each set of doors have?
questions.a: Each set of doors had two panels that swung on hinges.

questions.q: What was carved on the doors of the Holy Place?
questions.a: Cherubs and palm trees were carved on the doors of the Holy Place.

questions.q: What was carved on walls that spanned the entryway to its the sidewalls?
questions.a: There were carvings of palm trees on the walls that spanned the entryway to its the sidewalls.

commentary.text: After the prophet had observed the courts, he was brought to the temple. If we attend to instructions in the plainer parts of religion, and profit by them, we shall be led further into an acquaintance with the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.
